charts.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: This pack found no legal chart of accounts in Saint Christopher and Nevis, and opened neither the Companies Act nor the Income Tax Act: no section of either is cited. What the Value Added Tax Act, 2010 asks of a registered person is a tax invoice (s. 43) and records kept for six years (s. 79). This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of a statement of financial position and an income statement presented in the manner of IFRS for SMEs, which is a choice of this pack and not a text the country imposes. The settlement account of the VAT return (2100, refundable 1172) is distinct from the accounts the tax posts to (2101, 2102 and 2103 collected, 1170 and 1171 recoverable). See README.md

numbering.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2010, s. 43 — tax invoices and sales receipts (a registered supplier issues one original tax invoice for each taxable supply, in the form and with the information the regulations prescribe), and s. 44 — tax credit and debit notes. The Act, as read for this pack, does not say that the series of invoice numbers may have no gap, which is why `numbering` is `sequential` and not `gapless`; `number_format` is a convention this pack proposes. The particulars of a tax invoice are in the regulations and are not printed as mentions

payment_terms.legal_reference: No text of Saint Christopher and Nevis read for this pack sets a payment term between two businesses or a rate of interest on a commercial debt paid late: the interest of 1.25 % a month (s. 42) is a charge on the taxable person towards the Comptroller, not a term between two businesses. `legal_payment_days` and `late_payment_reference` are empty

tax_point.legal_reference: Value Added Tax Act, 2010, s. 35 — a supply occurs on the earliest of the date the goods are delivered or made available or the performance of the services begins, the date an invoice is issued and the date a payment is received (the section was read in its opening lines only: the particular cases are not modelled). `earliest_of_delivery_or_payment` is the nearest value of the closed vocabulary and is to be checked against s. 35 by a reviewer

einvoicing.legal_reference: No text of Saint Christopher and Nevis read for this pack obliges a business to issue or accept an electronic invoice: the Value Added Tax Act, 2010, s. 43 asks for a tax invoice in the form the regulations prescribe, without naming a platform, a format or a Peppol profile. No Peppol authority for the Federation was looked for. `profile`, `party_scheme` and `vat_scheme` are null: there is no domestic profile to name

not_taxed.legal_reference: Not modelled, and not a finding that the service is untaxed. The Value Added Tax Act, 2010, s. 26(1)(b) charges 17 % on imported services other than exempt ones, and s. 11 makes the person liable under s. 25(2)(c) furnish an import declaration and pay the tax within fifteen calendar days after the tax period in which the services were imported. The pack carries no code for this self-assessment (the tax would be both collected and deducted, and the declaration line was not found): such a purchase is entered with KN-P-EX and the user, with their accountant, accounts for the tax outside the pack. See README.md
